Sample.evidence_source: [/page/7/Text/7] Each treatment programme consisted of eight, weekly, one hour group sessions conducted by the same psychologist (a second year postgraduate clinical psychology trainee). Children attended sessions at their own schools in small groups of four to six children.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/2] Social Competence Training (SCT). The SCT programme was designed to teach overt social skills, cognitive restructuring, and interpersonal problem solving skills which would be used in problematic social situations identified by the children in the groups. The content of the SCT was adapted from programmes outlined by Camp and Bash (1981), Spivack and Shure (1978), Rathjen and Foreyt (1980), Spence (1980) and techniques based on adult Cognitive Therapy (Beck, Rush, Shaw and Emery, 1979).

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/7/Text/7] All children were given the same explanation for their inclusion in a group, namely that the experimenter was trying to look at ways of helping children feel better about themselves and their lives.
